result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.greedy_node_swap_bipartition()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Split the nodes into two communities by greedily moving nodes to raise modularity. twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.greedy_node_swap_bipartition()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Split the nodes into two communities by greedily moving nodes to raise modularity. title: >- [Graph.greedy_node_swap_bipartition()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Split the nodes into two communities by greedily moving nodes to raise modularity. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Split the nodes into two communities by greedily moving nodes to raise modularity. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L36674-L36779){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.greedy_node_swap_bipartition( init_split=None, max_iter=10, weighted=None, seed=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Greedy node-swap bipartition](../assets/graphs/greedy-node-swap-bipartition.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Two squares with a diagonal, A, B, C, D and E, F, G, H, joined by the edges D to E and C to F. Left, the starting split you pass, A, B, E, F (teal) against C, D, G, H (violet), cuts 8 edges, in the accent color, and has modularity -0.167. Right, after moving the nodes that raise modularity most, the halves are A, B, C, D and E, F, G, H, with only D to E and C to F cut and a modularity of 0.333." width="100%"} Starting from a split, each pass moves every node to the other side once, always choosing the move that raises modularity the most (or lowers it the least), and keeps the best split seen during the pass. Passes repeat until one brings no improvement. Allowing temporarily worse moves lets it escape some local optima, in the spirit of Kernighan-Lin, but without balancing the sizes: the communities may have any size. It is a simple way to refine a two-community split, such as one from `spectral_modularity_bipartition()`. Without `init_split=`, the start is a random half of the nodes; use `seed=` for reproducible results. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [init_split]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [tuple[list, list] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional starting split as two lists of nodes (IDs or labels) covering every node. [max_iter]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[10]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of passes (default 10). [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use edge weights in the modularity. If `None` (default), follows the graph's `weighted` flag. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Random seed for the starting half. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [tuple[set[int], set[int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The two communities as sets of node IDs (the first evolves from `init_split[0]` when a split is given). ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed, `init_split` is not a split of all nodes into two disjoint sets, or `max_iter` is negative. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Moving node $u$ from side $s$ to side $o$ changes modularity by $(k_{u,o} - k_{u,s}) / m + k_u (d_s - d_o - k_u) / 2m^2$, where $k_{u,X}$ is $u$'s edge weight to side $X$ (its self-loops left out), $k_u$ its degree, $d_X$ the total degree of side $X$ and $m$ the total edge weight. Gains are updated incrementally, so a pass costs $O(V^2 + E)$. Ties go to the lowest node ID. Follows NetworkX's `greedy_node_swap_bipartition` with these differences: NetworkX returns the split from before its last pass (so `max_iter=1` returns the starting split unchanged), whereas this returns the best split found; it accepts gains that are only rounding error (which can swap the two sides); it uses unweighted modularity and Python's global random state; it counts a self-loop's neighbor as being on its own side; and it accepts directed graphs. An edgeless graph returns the starting split. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Two triangles joined by an edge are separated: ::: {#13e36d26 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph().add_barbell_graph(3, 0, label=False) g.greedy_node_swap_bipartition(seed=1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ({4, 5, 6}, {1, 2, 3}) ``` ::: ::: Refining a split of the karate club: ::: {#af90f6f0 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} g = ec.karate_club() left, right = g.greedy_node_swap_bipartition(init_split=g.spectral_modularity_bipartition()) len(left), len(right), round(g.modularity([left, right]), 4) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (17, 17, 0.3718) ``` ::: :::
